name: Abū Ḥanīfa Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Dīnawarī
summary: Scholar of Dīnawar learned in grammar, language, geometry, arithmetic and astronomy, author of Kitāb al-Nabāt and al-Akhbār al-ṭiwāl; the print misnames him 'ibn al-Sikkīt'.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls Abū Ḥanīfa a man of many sciences, grammar, language, geometry, arithmetic and astronomy among them, and trustworthy in what he transmitted, and lists his books on the mistakes of common speech, on poetry and the poets, on eloquence and on the rains, among others.
He lived in Dīnawar and died in 282/895 (TDV). His Kitāb al-Nabāt, on plants, and al-Akhbār al-ṭiwāl, a history, are his best-known works.
uncertain: The print's heading and text call him 'Aḥmad ibn al-Sikkīt'; the man is Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Dīnawarī. Ibn al-Anbārī gives no year of death.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 305–306
Dîneverî, Ebû Hanîfe, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
